text.p: - Swiss pharmaceuticals group Novartis said on Tueaday that it will acquire the crop protection activities of U.S. chemical group Merck for 1.3 billion Swiss francs. Novartis announced it will also cut some 500 jobs in the pharma production in Basle. - A fourth Swiss TV channel will start on September 1 with a new concept under the new name of SF 2, featuring cinema films, sports, and programmes for young people.

- Iwan Rickerbacher, former general secretary of the Christian Democrats, predicts a gloomy future for his party. Within the realm of the three Swiss conservative parties, the Christian Democrats will have the worst chances to remain a major player, Rickenbacher said.

- Switzerland plans to intensify its search for personal fonds of Zaire President Mobutu after an informal search by large Swiss banks delivered no results. - Klaus Mueller, reponsible for planning a hospital in Basle, said in an interview different stages in treatments of patients with chronic diseases should be networked and better coordinated to improve service and lower costs.

- The Zurich high court ruled that Swiss supermarket chain Denner may continue with its comparative advertising campaigns. Rivals Migros and Coop said Denner's ads were missleading since they did not compare prices of comparable products.

- The European Union (EU) on Tuesday demanded new concessions from Switzerland with regard to Swiss Alpine traffic. The Swiss government said it will first examine the domestic political feasabilty of the EU proposals, which will delay negotiations.
